Cauda Equina Syndrome: sensory deficits in the lower extremities
motor deficits in the lower extremities
Urinary symptoms: hesitancy, frequency, nocturia, poor stream, sensation of incomplete emptying, possible intermittent retention, and urge incontinence for 2 years
Chief complaint: diarrhea and fecal incontinence for 2 months
Clinical examination: reduced resting and squeeze anal tone
Newly developed mild lower limb numbness when sitting, which resolved upon walking
MRI of the spine: lesion just distal to the conus, causing the roots of the cauda equina to be displaced peripherally at the level of L1/2

top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The patient's symptoms of urinary dysfunction, bowel dysfunction, and mild lower limb numbness, combined with the MRI findings of a lesion distal to the conus displacing the cauda equina roots, are consistent with Cauda Equina Syndrome. The reduced anal tone and absence of other explanatory conditions also support this diagnosis.
